note: JSON text to CBOR (RFC 8949) bytes by a private writer primitive over the shared json:parse. Deterministic encoding (section 4.2.1), documented in the op: shortest integer heads, a number with a fraction or exponent in the shortest of half, single and double that holds it exactly (1.0 is f93c00), definite lengths only, map keys sorted bytewise by their encoding, integers outside -2^64..2^64-1 as bignums (tags 2 and 3). CyberChef (the cbor npm package) writes maps in insertion order and floats as doubles; this is a deliberate difference and the bytes can differ for the same JSON. Added parameter typed-objects (off by default, as CyberChef): reads back the shapes cbor:decode writes ({"type":"Buffer","data":[...]} as a byte string, {"tag":N,"value":V} as a tag, {"simple":N}), so bytes and tags can be written at all. Nesting deeper than 64 levels is E_COERCE. Vectors from Python cbor2 (canonical) and RFC 8949 Appendix A. The CyberChef behaviour described here is from memory, not checked against 11.5.0 until the WP 5.59 cross-check.

CBOR (RFC 8949) bytes to JSON text by a private reader primitive and the shared json:stringify. All major types, indefinite lengths, half, single and double floats, big integers (tags 2 and 3 are exact integers). Bytes are shown as CyberChef shows the Buffer of the cbor npm package through JSON.stringify: {"type":"Buffer","data":[...]}; tags 0 and 1 are ISO 8601 dates with three fractional digits (a Date's toJSON); every other tag is {"tag":N,"value":V}; undefined, NaN and the infinities are null (as JSON.stringify writes them); a simple value other than false, true, null and undefined is {"simple":N}. A map key that is not text is written as the text of an integer, float, boolean or null, any other key and a repeated key are E_COERCE (JavaScript's Map would show as {}). Deliberate strictness: exactly one data item (bytes after it, empty input, truncation, invalid UTF-8, reserved heads, a break outside an indefinite item and nesting deeper than 64 levels are E_COERCE with the offset); a length is only compared with the bytes left. Floats stay floats (1.0). Added parameter indent (default 4, as CyberChef's JSON output, 0 for compact text). Vectors from Python cbor2 and RFC 8949 Appendix A; the CyberChef layout is from memory and not checked until the WP 5.59 cross-check.

JSON text to MessagePack bytes, written from the specification (no library) by a private writer primitive. Each value in the shortest format that holds it: positive integers as uint, negative as int (-2^63..2^64-1, else E_COERCE), a number with a fraction or exponent as float 32 when exact, else float 64, text as fixstr/str 8/16/32, arrays and maps in the order given. CyberChef (notepack.io) differs in places (for example it writes every float as float 64 and has no timestamps); the bytes can differ for the same JSON. Added parameter typed-objects (off by default): reads back the shapes msgpack:decode writes, {"type":"Buffer","data":[...]} as bin, {"ext":N,"data":<Buffer>} as an extension and {"timestamp":"<ISO 8601>"} as the shortest timestamp extension (32, 64 or 96 bits). Nesting deeper than 64 levels is E_COERCE. Vectors from Python msgpack (the float rule applied per value). The CyberChef behaviour is from memory, not checked until the WP 5.59 cross-check.

MessagePack bytes to JSON text by a private reader primitive. Every format of the specification: nil, booleans, all integer widths (exact), float 32 and 64, str (strict UTF-8), bin, array, map, fixext and ext 8/16/32, and the timestamp extension (type -1: 32, 64 and 96 bits, shown as ISO 8601 text with three fractional digits, more only when the nanoseconds need them). Binary strings are shown as the Buffer JSON.stringify writes ({"type":"Buffer","data":[...]}); other extensions as {"ext":N,"data":<Buffer>}; NaN and the infinities are null. A map key that is not text is written as the text of an integer, float, boolean or nil, any other key and a repeated key are E_COERCE. Deliberate strictness: exactly one object, the unused code 0xc1, truncation, invalid UTF-8, a bad timestamp and nesting deeper than 64 levels are E_COERCE with the offset. Added parameter indent (default 4, 0 for compact text). Vectors from Python msgpack. The CyberChef layout is from memory, not checked until the WP 5.59 cross-check.

JSON text to one AMF0 or AMF3 value (Adobe's specifications), by a private writer primitive. Parameter format AMF0 (the default) or AMF3, as CyberChef's options. AMF0: every number as a double, text as a string (long string above 65535 bytes), arrays as strict arrays, objects as anonymous objects, null as null. AMF3: integers from -2^28 to 2^28-1 as AMF3 integers, other numbers as doubles, text as a string, arrays as dense arrays, objects as dynamic anonymous objects. No reference tables are written, byte arrays, dates and typed objects cannot be written (JSON has no such values), an empty property name and nesting deeper than 64 levels are E_COERCE. Vectors built by hand from the specifications and checked against the amfy library. The CyberChef behaviour is from memory, not checked until the WP 5.59 cross-check.

One AMF0 or AMF3 value to JSON text by a private reader primitive. Parameter format AMF0 (default) or AMF3. Whole doubles up to 2^53 are integers, other numbers floats, NaN and the infinities null; undefined, null and the AMF0 unsupported marker are null; dates are ISO 8601 text; typed objects, ECMA arrays and AMF3 arrays with named keys are objects (the class name is dropped); byte arrays are {"type":"Buffer","data":[...]}; the AMF3 vectors are arrays and the dictionary an object. String, object and trait references are followed and the shared values copied under the value budget (a reference to an object still being read, a cycle, is E_COERCE because JSON cannot show it); the AMF0 avmplus marker switches to AMF3. Only one value is read, not an AMF packet with headers and messages. Deliberate strictness: the movieclip, recordset and externalizable markers, bad references, truncation, bytes after the value, invalid UTF-8, repeated keys and nesting deeper than 64 levels are E_COERCE with the offset. Added parameter indent (default 4). Vectors built by hand from the specifications and checked against amfy. The CyberChef layout is from memory, not checked until the WP 5.59 cross-check.

Avro Object Container Files (Apache Avro 1.11) to JSON text: the container is walked by a private header primitive, the data by a private datum decoder, the codec choice and the deflate codec (the deflate words, so the output budget applies) in FL. The schema comes from the file header (named types, namespaces, recursion, unions, logical types shown as their underlying values). Codecs null and deflate; any other (snappy, zstandard, bzip2, xz, lz4) is E_COERCE naming it. Parameter force-valid-json as CyberChef: off, one JSON record per line; on, one JSON array. A long is an exact integer, float and double are numbers, bytes and fixed are {"type":"Buffer","data":[...]} (avsc shows the Buffer through JSON.stringify), a union is the value of its branch (not wrapped). Added parameter indent (default 0, one line per record). Deliberate strictness: sync markers are checked, bytes after the last block, bad varints, out-of-range indices and nesting deeper than 64 levels are E_COERCE with the offset; a block's count of data of no bytes is metered against the value limit. Vectors from Python fastavro and containers built by hand from the specification. The CyberChef layout is from memory, not checked until the WP 5.59 cross-check.

A run of tag-length-value elements to JSON text by a private walk primitive. Parameters as CyberChef: tag bytes (default 1), length bytes (default 1), BER lengths (default off: short form below 128, long form 128 plus a count of up to 6 length bytes; the indefinite form and 0xff are E_COERCE). Output: an array of {"type":hex,"length":n,"value":hex} (this layout, with hex strings, is from memory and not checked against CyberChef until the WP 5.59 cross-check). Elements are not opened. Deliberate strictness: a header or value that runs past the data is E_COERCE with the offset; widths are 1 to 16 (tag) and 1 to 8 (length), E_RANGE otherwise. Added parameter indent (default 4). Vectors assembled with Python from (tag, value) lists.

Text, not HTML: three lines, Offset 0 (aligned): ..., Offset 1: ..., Offset 2: ..., the Base64 of the data behind 0, 1 and 2 other bytes. Written in FL over the base64 primitive and a 256-byte translation table. The characters that depend on the unknown bytes are left out; with show-variable on (the default, as CyberChef's Show variable chars and padding) the one character that depends on both, the last character when the data stops inside a group, and the padding are kept (CyberChef colours them; text cannot, so nothing marks them). Parameters as CyberChef: alphabet (ranges such as A-Za-z0-9+/=, 64 or 65 characters), show variable chars and padding, input type (raw, hex, base64; raw is the bytes). Added checks: the alphabet must be 64 or 65 different ASCII characters (E_RANGE), invalid hex or Base64 input is E_COERCE. The exact text of CyberChef's output is from memory (the labels, the trimming), not checked until the WP 5.59 cross-check. Vector values from Python base64.

JSON text to Rison, O-Rison or A-Rison by a private writer primitive: one op with a mode parameter (rison, o-rison, a-rison) for CyberChef's Encode, Encode Object and Encode Array. Rules of rison.js: !t !f !n, !(a,b) arrays, (k:v) objects with sorted keys (by UTF-16 code unit), bare identifiers or single-quoted strings with ' and ! escaped by !, numbers as JavaScript prints them without the + (an integer in full digits, so 1.0 is 1). O-Rison of a non-object and A-Rison of a non-array are E_COERCE; nesting deeper than 64 levels is E_COERCE. Vectors from Python prison and the rison.js rules (numbers derived by hand).

Rison, O-Rison and A-Rison text to JSON text by a private reader primitive, mode parameter as in the encoder. White space is allowed around the text only; integers without fraction or exponent are exact, a repeated key, a bad number, an unknown ! form, an unterminated string or list, text after the value and nesting deeper than 64 levels are E_COERCE with the offset. Added parameter indent (default 4). Vectors from Python prison.

An outline of an Apple property list by a private reader primitive that builds the text: { } for a dictionary with one key => value line per entry, [ ] for an array, four spaces per level, a nested container opening on the line of its key, scalars as text (dates as ISO 8601, data as Base64). The exact layout of CyberChef's output is from memory (the => separator and the indentation) and is not checked until the WP 5.59 cross-check. XML property lists (comments, CDATA, entities, doctype) as CyberChef; as an addition binary lists (bplist00) are read too. Deliberate strictness: an unknown element, a key without a value, a mismatched tag, text after the plist, a damaged binary list (offsets, references, counts, cycles) and nesting deeper than 64 levels are E_COERCE with the offset. Vectors from Python plistlib with the outline rendered by an independent function.

A QR Code Model 2 encoder written from ISO/IEC 18004 (numeric, alphanumeric and byte mode chosen for the whole text, versions 1 to 40, error correction L, M, Q and H, Reed-Solomon, the eight masks with the penalty rules of 7.8.3; the module matrix equals python-qrcode's for the 233 inputs tried) with the writers in primitives and the PNG file in FL over the deflate and crc words. Formats: svg (the default here; CyberChef's is PNG, but Forge cannot show images yet), text (two characters a module) and a 1-bit PNG. Parameters as CyberChef: module size (default 5), margin in modules (default 4), error correction (default M). Not provided: JPEG, EPS and PDF output (no image library is in scope; JPEG is not a sensible format for a QR code), kanji mode and ECI headers (UTF-8 bytes are written without an ECI header, as most generators do), Micro QR and mixed-mode segments (one mode for the whole text, so the code can be larger than a mixed-mode encoder's). Empty text, text that does not fit version 40 and parameters out of range are E_RANGE. Vectors from python-qrcode (single mode, auto version and mask), the ISO example codewords, and the PNG decoded with Pillow and the host's zlib.
